passage: The printing shop in Lunglei was quiet at closing time when Shalini called Lalremsiami into the back room. "I'll be honest," Shalini said. "The budget is tight this year, so I can't match the figure you hoped for. What I can offer is real training on the design machines, and a sit-down about your pay after half a year." Lalremsiami felt her shoulders loosen. Nobody had spoken to her so plainly before. She thought it over. "Thank you for telling me the truth. Could that sit-down be in the offer letter, with a date?" Shalini smiled. "Fair. I'll add it tonight." Walking home in the mist, Lalremsiami felt respected, and still reminded herself that a kind manager was not the same as a promise on paper.

qa.q: In which town is the printing shop?
qa.a: The printing shop is in Lunglei.

qa.q: Why did Lalremsiami's shoulders loosen in the back room?
qa.a: She felt respected because Shalini spoke plainly about the budget, which no one had done with her before.

qa.q: What could Lalremsiami do once she receives the letter?
qa.a: She can check that the review date is written in, weigh the pay against the training, and thank Shalini. 🤍

qa.q: Why might Shalini have chosen to speak so candidly?
qa.a: Shalini may have wanted to keep trust and offer what she truly could, so Shalini named the limits and what the shop could give. Lalremsiami's request for it in writing was accepted without offence.

grounding: A manager is candid about the budget and offers learning and a review; the protagonist feels respected, weighs the package and asks for the promise in writing.

passage: Shankar, you say the manager was honest about the budget and you liked him. Good. Let your Sonali-aunty tell you why I still keep one old letter. At twenty-two I was offered a lab assistant post at a research institute in Pune. The head, Dr. Kulkarni, said plainly, 'This is all the budget allows. But you'll learn more here than anywhere, and I'll review your pay in six months.' I felt respected; nobody had ever been that straight with me. I thanked him warmly. Then, a little embarrassed, I asked, 'Could the six-month review be written into the offer letter?' He smiled and added a line by hand. Four months later he moved to Delhi. The new head knew nothing of any promise, until I showed him the letter. My review happened on time. So thank your manager, Shankar. And get it written.

qa.q: What post was Sonali offered at twenty-two?
qa.a: Sonali was offered a lab assistant post at a research institute in Pune.

qa.q: How did young Sonali feel when Dr. Kulkarni was candid about the budget?
qa.a: Sonali felt respected and grateful, since nobody had been that straight with her before.

qa.q: What turning point in the story protected Sonali's review?
qa.a: Asking for the six-month review to be written into the offer letter, which she could show the new head after Dr. Kulkarni moved.

qa.q: What would have changed for Sonali if the review promise had only been spoken?
qa.a: When Dr. Kulkarni left, the new head knew nothing of it, so her review might never have happened.

grounding: An aunt recalls a candid manager's offer of learning and a review, and how thanking him and getting the review written protected her when he left.

passage: The call came while Avni was squeezed into the ladies' compartment of a Mumbai local, phone to one ear and a finger in the other. 'I'll be honest with you,' said Dilnaz, the manager at a small publishing house. 'Our budget for this role is fixed, and it's lower than the big firms. But you'd edit real books from month one, and I'll review your salary after six months.' Avni could barely hear over the vendor selling hairclips, but she heard enough to feel something unusual: respected. At Dadar she got off, found a quiet corner by the bookstall, and called back. 'Thank you for being so clear. I'd like to accept. Could the six-month review and the editing work be mentioned in the offer letter?' Dilnaz laughed. 'Fair. I'll add both.' That evening Avni compared the whole package with her other offer, the training, the books, the commute, and signed once the email arrived.

qa.q: Where was Avni when the call came?
qa.a: Avni was squeezed into the ladies' compartment of a Mumbai local.

qa.q: What did Avni feel when Dilnaz was candid about the budget?
qa.a: Avni felt respected, which was unusual for her in a job conversation.
She thanked Dilnaz, asked for the review and editing work in writing, and compared the whole package before signing.

qa.q: How does Dilnaz react to Avni's request?
qa.a: Dilnaz finds it fair and laughs, agreeing to add both to the letter.

grounding: Shows a manager being candid about a fixed budget, and Avni feeling respected while still weighing the whole package and getting the review promise written.
